transcript_window.text: And the last time it was amended was under the Patriot Act.

so amendments, if you ever read them in Congress when they pass laws, they'll say in Section 2709, after the third paragraph insert these two or three more paragraphs that now, know, add additional meaning or things like that.
And so I started to understand that in order to really grasp the meaning of Section 2709, you'd have to read all the different amendments that had ever happened and then piece it all together.
And you'd probably really need to go a law library.
And I didn't know how to do that research.
And the executive order, there was some information about it, but not enough for me to truly understand what it implied, what it meant.
And I felt really stuck at that point.
I would be too.
The Patriot Act was passed after two planes flew into buildings in New York City on 9 -11.
It was passed to try to stop terrorism.
And it granted the authority for the FBI to conduct searches without awards.
But was the FBI investigating a terrorist plot here?
Were they using this power as it was intended?
Nobody had ever seen these letters before because any time they were sent to someone, that person wasn't allowed to tell anyone else.
So these letters were entirely out of the public eye.
And the only people who knew they existed was the FBI and the people that the FBI gave it to.
The letter is called a national security letter or NSL.
And I think if I recall back, may have been dated like several days before when I actually got it.
So that's sort of to me implied that it wasn't super time sensitive.
wasn't like a nuclear bomb is gonna go off in 10 minutes.
You better do this or we're all gonna die.
was more like they weren't in such a hurry.
Like I think that it was dated like a week before they actually showed up.
I was like, okay.
So he sat down and looked at the letter closer.
his interpretation, this letter violated three of his constitutional rights.
The first amendment is your right to free speech.
This letter suppressed his speech.
wasn't allowed to talk about this letter.
